cohort.rule: nonblank finite latitude/longitude within geographic coordinate ranges, using frozen base CSV
cohort.relationshipToExistingEligible: same IDs for current snapshot; selected via coordinate availability rather than score/label
cohort.scope: Daegu reference pool fixed for this version; no top-N/recommended-industry-only subset; no local-filter refit

factorColumns.rentBurden: not exported; derive separately from frozen raw rent+management using baseline rule

data.inputValidity: scores finite in [0,100], no raw money-distance score mixing; listing IDs unique and joins exact
data.referenceDateForAge: retain baseline engine TODAY=2026-11-10; do not silently recalculate age using current date
data.precision: current exported scores rounded to 0.1 are baseline; recomputed rent burden rounded to same precision for main pilot; raw inputs retained

main.reason: existing demo/sensitivity/label-experiment comparison condition; not a statistically established typical budget
main.rentBurdenFormula: baseline interpolation: ratio <=0.5 =>100; 0.5<ratio<=1 =>160-120*ratio; above budget =>not a cost fitting observation
main.cohort: coordinate reference pool intersect affordability, then complete cases for all active cost factors
main.scoringFunction: existing v2; do not apply proposed converted-rent/percentile scheme

supplementary.interpretation: two-factor missing-budget case; not a complete replacement for 3-factor cost shares

supplementary.budgetRule: 25th/50th/75th percentiles of rent+management in fixed coordinate reference pool
supplementary.quantile: linear interpolation at (n-1)*p; finite nonnegative valid amounts only; deduplicate; require budget>0
supplementary.purpose: data-derived affordability scenarios; report separately; do not average into one universal vector

budget.managementMissing: reproduce baseline zero imputation, explicitly flag 1657/2717 missing in full source; a management-known subset rerun is sensitivity analysis only, not population truth
budget.negativeOrMissingRent: report invalid raw rent separately; do not silently create zero rent; unexpected raw conditions require input review
budget.otherGroups: fit on fixed coordinate cohort; do not refit merely because budget filter changes
budget.want: null; retain industry default area; alternative area conditions left to later sensitivity review

missingness.structuralAbsent: remove before group listwise deletion; reason recorded; not an observed zero score
missingness.ordinary: for each category-group fit on one complete-case cohort shared by all active columns; no pairwise deletion in CRITIC matrix; no zero/mean fill
missingness.productionScoring: retain baseline per-listing available-factor renormalization and separate data-coverage reporting; fitting deletion is not recommendation deletion

primaryNormalization.name: fixed_score_scale
primaryNormalization.reason: preserve team-defined existing 0-100 score scales while estimating within-group shares
primaryNormalization.differenceFromOriginal: original paper uses sample min-max. This adaptation must be named explicitly; no claim of fully identical original preprocessing

supplementaryNormalization.name: sample_minmax_weight_estimation_only
supplementaryNormalization.scope: same complete-case sample; weight-estimation normalization comparison; downstream baseline score functions remain unchanged
supplementaryNormalization.caution: different normalization may produce materially different weights

correlation.name: Pearson
correlation.negative: retain sign; do not silently use abs(r), clip negative correlations or drop a high-correlation criterion

method.rounding: retain full precision in future machine outputs; display percentages to 1 decimal with displayed-sum correction documented; no clipping to policy minimum/maximum

degenerate.constant: remove exactly constant columns from information-weight fit and record constant_on_reference_sample; do not interpret as globally irrelevant; candidate information weight zero only in this version, not automatically deployed
degenerate.allConstantOrZeroInformation: no CRITIC estimate; report cannot_estimate and comparison fallback existing normalized within-group shares; label fallback explicitly
degenerate.insufficientN: complete-case n<2 =>cannot_estimate; n>=2 only arithmetic feasibility, not statistical reliability
degenerate.oneActiveFactor: 100% arithmetic allocation; mark single_factor, not a learned importance result
degenerate.twoActiveFactors: if r<1 and both SD>0, common (1-r) cancels, so weights are proportional to SD; mark two_factor_sd_ratio. If perfect positive correlation leaves total information zero, cannot_estimate
degenerate.nearDegenerate: if SD or total information within numerical tolerance, mark diagnostic; do not invent epsilon weights
degenerate.nonfiniteOrOutOfRange: halt affected category-group fitting, report input invalidity

method.smallSampleReliability: report n and later bootstrap dispersion; no arbitrary n=30 guarantee

baselines: equal shares within each active group
preserved: same scenario filters/cohort for ranking comparisons
laterMetrics: group score and total score changes
top10/top50 retained; use min(K,n) and disclose cutoff ties
bootstrap weight dispersion and normalization/budget sensitivity
comparisons.eligibility: recompute factor coverage with each candidate within-group weight and original group weights; threshold=60 retained; report data-eligibility changes separately from rank changes on common eligible candidates
comparisons.interpretation: statistical combination rationale and stability only, not validated tenant preference or survival/rentability prediction

existingExperiment.labels: broker recommendation text, not observed good/bad
existingExperiment.handling: preserve; separate appendix/comparator, no automatic adoption or pooling into CRITIC

sources.title: Diakoulaki, Mavrotas & Papayannakis (1995), Determining objective weights in multiple criteria problems: The CRITIC method
sources.supports: sample minmax preprocessing, SD, correlation, information weight normalization; two-factor cancellation is our algebraic deduction

stageGate: This is stage2 method review only. Wait for user before implementing or calculating stage3 weights.
